body.x: InHandPlus (CEO Hwiwon Lee) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

InHandPlus has developed smart watches and AI-based medication management solutions to address subjects' low medication compliance in clinical trials. According to the company, their product optimizes global clinical trials by providing an accurate RWD (Real World Data) with AI smart watches to identify when and which medications patients are taking.

Being considered innovative in overcoming existing limitations simply with wearable devices, their solutions have won the Innovation Award in this CES proving the technological excellence. The solution features great user convenience, excellent data accuracy, and high-level versatility to analyze various types of medicines.

In clinical trials, issues of poor subject compliance have existed due to the lack of an accurate solution for medication management. In addition, the need to collect RWD has emerged after the breakout of the COVID-19 pandemic for remote or decentralized clinical trials that are on the rise. Considering this trend, InHandPlus has been working to develop a solution that can perfectly respond to this demand.

In fact, their solutions are already used in clinical trials in South Korea, attracting large CROs as investors. The business has also been selected for Bayer and Merck's Startup Accelerator program, and has partnered with various pharmaceutical corporations and hospitals.

According to a representative from InHandPlus, “We are participating in the largest CES in the world in order to seek partnerships with multinational pharmaceutical businesses, CROs, hospitals and insurers.” They added, “We are also interested in informing global investors about the innovativeness of our technology so that we can attract additional investments.”

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
